# cqrlog

**Full-featured station log with a database behind it and rig control in front**

- **Version recorded:** 2.5.2
- **Categories:** `logging`, `rig-control`
- **Upstream:** <https://www.cqrlog.com>

## What it does

Keeps the station log in a MariaDB database rather than a file, which is what lets it answer questions a flat log cannot: worked-before checks across every band and mode at once, DXCC and IOTA award tracking, grey-line and beam-heading display for the callsign currently in the entry field. It drives the rig through hamlib, uploads to LoTW, eQSL and ClubLog, and imports and exports ADIF.

## Why you would want it

It is the heaviest of the general-purpose Linux logs and the one to choose when the log is the centre of the station rather than a record kept after the fact. If what you want is a log that opens instantly and stays out of the way, xlog or KLog will suit you better; if you want award tracking that is actually correct, this is the one that does it.

## Before it will work

A MariaDB server. The package depends on the client and server core libraries and recommends the server itself, which our apt backend installs because it does not suppress Recommends. A callsign certificate is needed before LoTW upload will work, which comes from TQSL rather than from here.

## How it installs

- apt: `cqrlog`
  - Present on every target except Kali, measured across all six on 2026-08-28. The block is left unconditional rather than excluding Kali by selector: apt answers the question correctly and currently at plan time, where a selector would encode one evening's measurement and go stale the day Kali picks the package up.

## Known problems

Installed with Recommends suppressed it will start and then fail to connect to a database that is not running -- an error that reads as a configuration problem rather than a missing package. It is a Free Pascal application built with Lazarus and uses GTK 2, which is unmaintained upstream; it works, and it will not gain a modern theme or fractional scaling. On a HiDPI display expect small text that no setting inside the program fixes.

## Keeping it current

- probe: apt policy
- strategy: apt_upgrade
